article_title: Tracking Behavioral Patterns among Students in an Online Educational System
citation: Stephan Lorenzen, Niklas Hjuler, Stephen Alstrup. (2019). Tracking Behavioral Patterns among Students in an Online Educational System. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08937
title: Weighted non-negative matrix factorization for soft clustering of student log behavior over weekly periods
description: The article uses weighted non-negative matrix factorization (WNMF) as a soft clustering method: features aggregated per student per weekly activity period form a matrix X approximated as UV, where V gives feature importance per cluster and U gives each student-period's membership in each cluster. Missing values (e.g. absent quiz scores) are handled via a binary weight matrix, and clusters are rescaled so rows of V sum to one. The method is applied once over two years of Clio Online data, allowing tracking of behavior at individual and system-wide levels.
requirements: A set of activity/performance features aggregated per student per weekly period, and a chosen number of clusters k selected by the decrease in error between successive k values
constraints: The number of clusters is fixed in this setting; the article notes an adaptive clustering strategy might be preferable since clusters may change over time
Individual behavioral change was not directly analyzed due to privacy concerns
target_learners: primary school students in Denmark using the Clio Online system
target_learning_goals: understanding student activity patterns and their relation to performance across subjects and Bloom's taxonomy levels
examples: Applied to 14,810 students and approximately 677,000 student entries across 112 weekly periods, yielding five behavior clusters in the performance experiment and three subject clusters in the Bloom-level experiment
key_sources: Stephan Lorenzen, Niklas Hjuler, Stephen Alstrup. (2019). Tracking Behavioral Patterns among Students in an Online Educational System. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08937
